The frontend onSuccess then shows a 'guests_added' success toast, so a total email-delivery failure is reported as success with no diagnostic info. This is a real, diff-introduced behavior gap, though one could argue the DB update itself succeeded; classified as a defect with moderate confidence.

judged_text: The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the caught err and logs only the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails', then the handler returns success. When the email send fails, the organizer still sees the 'Guests added' success toast while no attendee was notified, and operations has no error message or stack trace in the logs to diagnose the delivery failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows `err` and logs only a static message, then the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This is verifiably poor observability and can hide delivery failures, but it doesn’t break the core mutation outcome shown in the diff (guests are still added to the booking and calendars are updated), and the UI toast `t("guests_added")` reflects the mutation success rather than explicitly guaranteeing email delivery.
